{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Vartkess Ara Apkarian''' (born 1955) is an Armenian-American [[Physical chemistry|physical chemist]] and a Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of California, Irvine]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chem.umn.edu/event/department-seminar-professor-vartkess-ara-apkarian|title=Department Seminar: Professor Vartkess "Ara" Apkarian|date=February 5, 2018|website=Department of Chemistry}}</ref>

==Career==
{{Moresources | section|date=February 2024}}
He is the Director of [[Center for Chemistry at the Space-Time Limit]], a [[National Science Foundation]] [[Center for Chemical Innovation]]. He graduated from [[University of Southern California]] with B.S. degrees in Chemistry followed by Ph.D. degree in chemistry from [[Northwestern University]]. Following a postdoctoral fellowship at Cornell University, he joined the University of California as Chemistry faculty in 1983. He served as the Chair of the Chemistry Department (2004-2007) at UC Irvine.
[[File:Vartkess A Apkarian.jpg|thumb|Vartkess Apkarian at CaSTL Annual Meeting]]
He is a Foreign Member of the [[Armenian National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences of Armenia]], and a Fellow of [[American Physical Society]], [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]s. His teaching and research has been recognized with awards including the [[Humboldt Prize]] (1996), USC Distinguished Alumnus (2007), Charles Bennett Service Through Chemistry Award of ACS (2008) ACS Award in Experimental Physical Chemistry (2014), Honorary Doctorate from the [[University of Jyväskylä]], Finland (2016).<ref>{{Cite web |title=UC Irvine - Faculty Profile System |url=https://faculty.uci.edu/profile/?facultyId=7203 |access-date=2026-02-11 |website=faculty.uci.edu}}</ref>

His recent scientific contributions include creating a single-molecule [[sensor]]<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Yampolsky |first=Steven |last2=Fishman |first2=Dmitry A. |last3=Dey |first3=Shirshendu |last4=Hulkko |first4=Eero |last5=Banik |first5=Mayukh |last6=Potma |first6=Eric O. |last7=Apkarian |first7=Vartkess A. |date=August 2014 |title=Seeing a single molecule vibrate through time-resolved coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nphoton.2014.143 |journal=Nature Photonics |language=en |volume=8 |issue=8 |pages=650–656 |doi=10.1038/nphoton.2014.143 |issn=1749-4893|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and developing tools to confine the light to atomic dimensions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lee|first=Joonhee|last2=Tallarida|first2=Nicholas|last3=Chen|first3=Xing|last4=Liu|first4=Pengchong|last5=Jensen|first5=Lasse|last6=Apkarian|first6=Vartkess Ara|date=2017-11-28|title=Tip-Enhanced Raman Spectromicroscopy of Co(II)-Tetraphenylporphyrin on Au(111): Toward the Chemists' Microscope|journal=ACS Nano|volume=11|issue=11|pages=11466–11474|doi=10.1021/acsnano.7b06183|pmid=28976729|issn=1936-0851|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Yao |first=Rongyue |last2=Zhao |first2=Shihang |last3=Zhang |first3=Yuan |last4=Zheng |first4=Changlin |last5=Wang |first5=Luxia |date=2025-01-09 |title=Plexcitons in Bowtie Nanocavities–Quantum Dots Systems Studied by Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c02606 |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry C |volume=129 |issue=1 |pages=428–435 |doi=10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c02606 |issn=1932-7447|url-access=subscription }}</ref> His team visualized the internal structure of single molecules and imaging the [[Normal mode|normal vibrational modes]] of single molecules.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Apkarian|first=V.
